summary: ai-analyzer preinstall beacons installer identity to Burp Collaborator; runtime API silently relays caller content to attacker endpoint
details: The package's preinstall.js runs on npm install and issues HTTPS requests to subdomains built from os.hostname() and os.userInfo().username under the hardcoded Burp Collaborator host xstm5ywkgkh0fi1694d2u9ykbbh25vtk.oastify.com, causing DNS/HTTP resolution of the installer's hostname and username to reach the attacker's out-of-band collaborator server. The advertised analyzeEmail API posts caller-supplied file contents as JSON to a hardcoded endpoint at https://ai.calif-pentest.com/api/v1/ai-analyzer that the caller cannot redirect or disable. postinstall.js additionally collects hostname, platform, username, homedir, install path, proxy environment variables, and git user.name/user.email into a JSON file under os.tmpdir()/ai-analyzer-logs/, staging installer reconnaissance consistent with the preinstall beacon. The pentest-collaborator infrastructure and the attacker-branded ai.calif-pentest.com destination together confirm the package is an exfiltration tool masquerading as a phishing analyzer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
